newsitem.title: USA: Wet fields slow Missouri crop planting progress.
newsitem.headline: Wet fields slow Missouri crop planting progress.

text.p: Wet fields slowed crop planting in Missouri during the week ended Sunday, according to the weekly Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service report.

Corn was 22 percent planted versus 65 percent a year ago and 32 average. Planting was most advanced in the southeast and southwest districts, which were more than 70 percent planted, while elsewhere less than 15 percent was planted.
Grain sorghum was two percent planted versus six percent last year as well as the five-year average.
Cotton was three percent planted versus two percent a year ago and four percent for the five-year average.

Winter wheat improved slightly to 12 percent excellent, 51 good, 26 fair, 10 percent poor and one very poor. The most favorable ratings were in the north central, west central, east central and southwest districts and less favorable ratings were in the southeast and south central regions.
Six percent of wheat had headed versus none last year and four percent average.
Oat acreage was 86 percent planted, behind 99 percent a year ago but ahead of 80 average.
Topsoil moisture was rated three percent short, 56 adequate and 41 percent surplus.

Pasture and ranges were rated seven percent poor, 33 fair, 55 good and five excellent. Warm, sunny weather was needed to encourage pasture growth, which has been slowed by below-normal temperatures in recent weeks.
